messages.author: fb9338407f9d7bba
messages.subject: RSF error
parts:
Hi Chris,

I’m using rsf.select() and am running into an error code for a handful of my individuals. The error suggests that there are NA values for some sampled points. I confirmed that the rasters adequately cover the akde, so NAs are not being extracted from the raster.

I looked through the code for the rsf.select() and rsf.fit() functions to try and understand what is happening.

If I understand correctly, rsf.select() tries various models using the parameters from the previous model to inform the next model. What seems to be happening is that, in some cases, a model ends up with estimates of NaN or Inf for various parameters, and importantly for mu. This results in NaNs for x and y in DATA within rsf.select() and triggers the warning.

Does this interpretation sound correct? If so, do you have a recommendation for handling this? Would it be reasonable to select the best performing model from the ones that did work and didn’t result in NaNs or Inf? 

Thank you for your help!

-Stella

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: RSF error
parts:
Hi Stella,

I fixed rsf.select() on GitHub to not copy over NA coefficients from previous models.

I'd prefer not to get NA parameter estimates in the first place. So far, the only time I've seen this happen is when having too many categories in a categorical variable, so that there's no longer a functioning reference category being sampled. Outside of this, if you run into further issues, then I'd like to diagnose them, and you can feel free to send me a minimal working example to reproduce the issue.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: RSF error
parts:
Hi Stella,

From what I could see, the only issue was an incompatibility between the newer code and older fit objects. You can update older fit objects with the following code:

AKDE@CTMM$symmetry <- FALSE
AKDE@CTMM$ISO$symmetry <- FALSE
AKDE@CTMM$MLE$symmetry <- FALSE

CTMM$symmetry <- FALSE
CTMM$ISO$symmetry <- FALSE
CTMM$MLE$symmetry <- FALSE

Best,
Chris
